newsitem.title: BELGIUM: NATO DEFENCE MINISTERS MEET ON ALLIANCE FUTURE.
newsitem.headline: NATO DEFENCE MINISTERS MEET ON ALLIANCE FUTURE.

text.p: NATO defence ministers met on Thursday to plot the future of the Western alliance as it prepares to expand into former communist Europe and adapt itself for new roles in a post-Cold War European security order.
The meeting is the last one before a summit in Madrid in early July at which at least three former Warsaw Pact foes are expected to be asked to join the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO).

NATO sources say the ministers, however, are unlikely to be able to agree on final details of a reformed command structure, considered vital if the alliance is to be flexible enough to undertake more Bosnia-style peace missions.

They say the election in France of a socialist government has made it unlikely Paris will carry out earlier plans to reintegrate into the military wing it quit in 1966 in a row over U.S. dominance, previously considered to be the price for concessions by other allies on scrapping some commands.
The 16 allies are also set to debate ways of boosting cooperation with Russia now the former foes have agreed to create a standing NATO-Russia council, seen as Moscow's price for enlargement.

Washington is also expected to tell its allies that it would prefer to see enlargement restricted to only three new members, probably Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic, at least for the foreseeable future.
